note: The one place a written rule becomes an executable rule, for ANY domain built in this workspace — not just Vitalis. To govern a new lane (real estate, apparel, 75 Hard, Primerica), add an entry here. Do not write a second checker; builder-control/doctrine-check.cjs reads this file, the pre-commit hook runs it on every staged file, and CI reruns it server-side.
howToAddARule: id      — stable, greppable. It appears in the failure message.
scope   — glob(s) the rule applies to. A rule only fires on files it names, so a peptide rule never fires on a listing package.
forbid  — regex (JS source, no delimiters) for content that must NOT appear.
excludeScope — optional glob(s) that win over scope. Use it to keep a 'customer-facing' rule off build evidence, runtime logs and internal audits, which are not customer-facing.
exempt  — optional regex; when it matches the surrounding text the hit is ignored. Use it for the CORRECT neighbour of the rule, so the check does not fail correct writing.
canon   — the document that makes this a rule. Required. A failure that cannot cite its authority is not enforceable and will be argued with.
rule    — one plain sentence a person can act on without asking anybody.
severity— 'block' fails the gate; 'review' reports and does not fail. Use 'review' when the distinction genuinely needs human judgment.

rules.canon: memory/feedback_gate_pass_language_banned.md — gate-pass language BANNED without a verdict file
rules.rule: Do not write that a gate passed without the evidence next to it — the command, its exit status, or the verdict path. An unevidenced 'tests passed' is the sentence every theater incident is built on.
The partnering naturopath is "Dr. Vincent Lun". The casual form "Vinny" is verbal shorthand and must never appear on a document that leaves the building.

rules.canon: CLAUDE.md — "Do not use internal jargon in customer-facing text"
rules.rule: These are build-system words. A client reading them learns how the document was manufactured instead of what to do.

rules.forbid: \b(FDA|Health Canada|USDA|NIH|CDC|Food and Drug Administration)\b[^.]{0,60}?\b(approved|endorsed|backed|certified|recommends?|recommended|sanctioned)\b|\b(approved|endorsed|backed|certified|sanctioned)\b[^.]{0,60}?\b(FDA|Health Canada|USDA|NIH|CDC|Food and Drug Administration)\b
rules.canon: CLAUDE.md — "Keep North American government/regulatory agencies out of customer-facing peptide-value authority framing"
rules.rule: Naming a regulator as the reason a compound is worth taking borrows an authority it does not have. Stating a boundary ("not approved by...") is required and stays allowed.
